title: Famous Designers
headline: Do you know who designed that?
tagline: Chairs, logos, typefaces, and the people behind them.
intro: The things around you were all decided by someone: the chair, the letters on the sign, the shape of the bottle.
Forty cards on the designers whose decisions stuck, from the Bauhaus to the iPod.

verdicts.low: A moodboard, not yet a portfolio. Keep collecting.
verdicts.mid: A solid first draft. The kerning needs work.
verdicts.high: Portfolio-ready. Rams would give a small nod.

levels.name: Sketchbook
levels.tagline: Famous names and the objects everyone knows.

questions.prompt: Who designed this lounge chair?
questions.imageAlt: A low leather lounge chair with a matching ottoman, its shell in curved dark plywood.
questions.fact: Herman Miller has made the Eames Lounge Chair since 1956; its shell is molded plywood veneered in rosewood.

questions.prompt: Who led Apple's design team through the iMac, iPod and iPhone years?
questions.fact: Ive joined Apple in 1992 and ran its design studio from 1996 until he left in 2019.

questions.statement: Coco Chanel is credited with popularising the little black dress.
questions.fact: Vogue printed her plain black dress in 1926 and called it Chanel's Ford, a uniform for every woman.

questions.prompt: Dieter Rams spent most of his career designing for which company?
questions.fact: Rams led Braun's design department from 1961 to 1995 and wrote the ten principles of good design.

questions.prompt: Tap these chairs by the year they first went into production, earliest first.
questions.fact: Breuer's tubular steel came first; Panton's single piece of plastic took until 1967 to manufacture.

questions.prompt: Who drew this typeface?
questions.imageAlt: A type specimen: rows of clean sans-serif letters in black on white.
questions.fact: Miedinger drew Helvetica in 1957 with Eduard Hoffmann; it launched as Neue Haas Grotesk.

questions.statement: Philippe Starck designed the Juicy Salif lemon squeezer for IKEA.
questions.fact: The three-legged squeezer was made by Alessi in 1990; Starck sketched it on a pizzeria placemat.

questions.prompt: Who founded the school that built this in 1925?
questions.imageAlt: A white modernist building with a glass curtain wall and large lettering down its side.
questions.fact: Gropius founded the Bauhaus in Weimar in 1919 and designed its Dessau building himself.

questions.prompt: Who designed the London Underground map as a diagram rather than a geographic map?
questions.fact: Beck's 1933 diagram treated the network like an electrical circuit, with only horizontals, verticals and diagonals.

questions.prompt: Which fashion designer launched the New Look in 1947?
questions.fact: The nipped waist and full skirt used yards of fabric just as wartime rationing was ending.

levels.name: Studio
levels.tagline: Attributions, influences, and why things look the way they do.

questions.prompt: Which Apple product is often compared to Braun's 1958 T3 pocket radio?
questions.fact: The T3 was Dieter Rams' work; the iPod's white face and round wheel echo it almost line for line.

questions.statement: Ray Eames was Charles Eames' sister.
questions.fact: Ray Kaiser married Charles in 1941; their office credited every design to both of them.

questions.prompt: Tap these typefaces by release year, earliest first.
questions.fact: Renner's Futura, Miedinger's Helvetica, Frutiger's airport face, then Hoefler and Frere-Jones's Gotham.

questions.prompt: Marcel Breuer said the frame of this chair was inspired by what?
questions.imageAlt: A chair made of bent tubular steel with leather straps for the seat, back and arms.
questions.fact: Breuer's own Adler bicycle showed him in 1925 that bent steel tube could be light, strong and mass-produced.

questions.prompt: Who designed this chair, with Lilly Reich, for the 1929 German Pavilion in Barcelona?
questions.imageAlt: A low leather chair on two crossed, curved steel bars, with tufted cushions.
questions.fact: The chair was made for the Spanish king and queen to sit on at the pavilion's opening.

questions.statement: Massimo Vignelli designed the 1972 New York City subway map.
questions.fact: His diagram was replaced by a more geographic map in 1979, then revived online as the Weekender in 2011.

questions.prompt: Whose ten principles end with good design is as little design as possible?
questions.fact: Rams wrote the principles in the 1970s; the first is that good design is innovative.

questions.prompt: Saul Bass is best known for designing what?
questions.fact: Bass opened Vertigo and Anatomy of a Murder, and drew the logos of AT&T, United Airlines and Kleenex.

questions.prompt: Zaha Hadid was the first woman to win which prize, in 2004?
questions.fact: Her first built work was the Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein, finished in 1993.

questions.prompt: Which car did Giorgetto Giugiaro design?
questions.fact: The 1974 Golf was Giugiaro's; the DS was Flaminio Bertoni's, the 911 Butzi Porsche's, the Mini Alec Issigonis's.

levels.name: Atelier
levels.tagline: Exact years and deep cuts, against the clock.

questions.prompt: In which year did Dieter Rams and Hans Gugelot design this radiogram, nicknamed Snow White's Coffin?
questions.imageAlt: A white and pale wood radio and record player with a clear acrylic lid.
questions.fact: The transparent lid was a first for hi-fi, and it gave the SK 4 its nickname.

questions.prompt: How many stripes does Paul Rand's 1972 IBM logo have?
questions.fact: The stripes suggest speed and unify the three letters' widths; Rand had drawn a solid version in 1956.

questions.statement: Helvetica was released in 1957 under the name Neue Haas Grotesk.
questions.fact: It became Helvetica in 1960, from Helvetia, the Latin name for Switzerland, to sell abroad.

questions.prompt: Tap these designers by year of birth, earliest first.
questions.fact: Chanel 1883, Eames 1907, Rams 1932, Ive 1967: four generations of what a good object looks like.

questions.prompt: In which year did Yves Saint Laurent show Le Smoking, the tuxedo for women?
questions.fact: Helmut Newton's 1975 photograph for Vogue, in a Paris alley at night, made it an icon.

questions.prompt: Alvar Aalto designed this vase for which 1937 event?
questions.imageAlt: A clear glass vase with a wavy, free-form outline.
questions.fact: Iittala still blows the vase; its name, Savoy, comes from the Helsinki restaurant Aalto furnished.

questions.statement: Raymond Loewy designed the Volkswagen Beetle.
questions.fact: The Beetle was Ferdinand Porsche's; Loewy's cars were Studebakers, the 1953 Starliner and the 1963 Avanti.

questions.prompt: Who designed this, the first single-piece plastic chair?
questions.imageAlt: A glossy S-shaped chair moulded from one continuous piece, with no legs.
questions.fact: Vitra put the chair into production in 1967, after years of prototypes in fibreglass and foam.

questions.prompt: In which city did the Bauhaus close for good in 1933?
questions.fact: Weimar in 1919, Dessau from 1925, Berlin from 1932; the Nazis forced it shut the next year.

questions.prompt: Milton Glaser's I Love New York logo dates from which year?
questions.fact: Glaser sketched it in the back of a taxi with a red crayon, and did the job for free.

levels.name: Legend
levels.tagline: Every trick in the studio, on a ten-second clock.

questions.prompt: Who redesigned the Lucky Strike pack in 1940?
questions.fact: Loewy printed the target on both sides, so the logo showed whichever way the pack landed.

questions.statement: Eileen Gray's house E-1027 stands on the coast of Ireland.
questions.fact: It is at Roquebrune-Cap-Martin on the French Riviera; Le Corbusier later painted murals on its walls uninvited.

questions.prompt: Ettore Sottsass designed this portable typewriter for Olivetti in 1969. What is it called?
questions.imageAlt: A bright red portable typewriter in a matching red bucket case.
questions.fact: The Lettera 22 was Marcello Nizzoli's; Sottsass went on to found the Memphis Group in 1981.

questions.prompt: Tap these moments in order, earliest first.
questions.fact: 1919, 1925, 1972, 1981, 2001: from a school in Weimar to a thousand songs in your pocket.

questions.prompt: Adrian Frutiger designed the signage typeface for which airport?
questions.fact: Drawn for Roissy in 1975, the face was released to everyone as Frutiger in 1976.

questions.prompt: Who designed this chair for the SAS Royal Hotel in Copenhagen in 1958?
questions.imageAlt: A high-backed armchair whose shell curves around the sitter like a shell.
questions.fact: Jacobsen designed the whole hotel, down to the cutlery; the Egg and the Swan were made for its lobby.

questions.statement: Charlotte Perriand worked with Le Corbusier on the LC4 chaise longue.
questions.fact: Perriand joined his studio in 1927; the LC furniture is credited to Le Corbusier, Pierre Jeanneret and Perriand.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the phrase form follows function?
questions.fact: Sullivan wrote it in an 1896 essay on tall buildings; Wright had been his draftsman.

questions.prompt: Kenji Ekuan designed which tabletop object for Kikkoman in 1961?
questions.fact: The red-capped bottle has stayed in production, unchanged, for more than sixty years.

questions.prompt: Who drew the Nike swoosh in 1971?
questions.fact: Davidson, then a design student, was paid 35 dollars; Nike later gave her shares in the company.
